subject.title: WhatsApp inbound messages not received in k3s nested container (outbound works)

question: Should WhatsApp external-inbound loss be addressed with active liveness verification, provider-side reconnect backfill, explicit unrecoverable-gap diagnostics, or a combined policy?
rationale: Current main only covers Baileys-delivered reconnect `append` events, while the remaining no-upsert symptom spans provider history semantics, liveness, privacy, read receipts, and live WhatsApp proof.

options.title: Combined recovery design
options.body: Design a WhatsApp-plugin policy with active post-reconnect liveness, bounded monitored-chat backfill where reliable, and explicit warnings when messages cannot be recovered.

options.title: Warn-only diagnostics first
options.body: Add status and log diagnostics for inbound-stream gaps without replaying history until WhatsApp/Baileys backfill behavior is proven live.

options.title: Accept append-only scope
options.body: Declare the current bounded append catch-up behavior sufficient and close broader no-event recovery only after maintainers explicitly accept that remaining cases are outside scope.

recommendation.title: Combined recovery design
recommendation.body: Design a WhatsApp-plugin policy with active post-reconnect liveness, bounded monitored-chat backfill where reliable, and explicit warnings when messages cannot be recovered.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the durable inbound path and the partial-fix handoff that explicitly left the provider-side gap open.
